background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding.

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak. Led to discovery of the Bundibugyo strain.
Second documented outbreak. Contained within months.
Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history. Different species (Zaire ebolavirus), but the same geographic region and many of the same containment challenges (insecurity, mistrust, mobile populations).

why_this_matters: No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus.
The outbreak zone overlaps with active armed conflict in eastern DRC.
Cross-border spread to Uganda confirmed within days of first detection.
Healthcare worker deaths suggest hospital-based transmission and IPC gaps.
High positivity rate of initial samples implies underdetection — true caseload likely much higher.
